title: Add downgrade guard and Postgres schema migration hooks + backup/restore for Private Installer
author: Priya Menon
ci_status: pass (initial failed PG-migrate unit test, rerun passed)
description:
Motivation: Private deployments must support safe upgrades and guaranteed rollback for regulated customers. We observed two incidents where a user-initiated downgrade after a failed upgrade left the Postgres schema ahead of the application, causing runtime errors. This PR introduces a downgrade guard, explicit schema migration hooks, and an integrated backup/restore flow in the private-installer to prevent and recover from schema drift.

What this PR does: - Adds a downgrade guard that prevents downgrades when non-reversible schema changes are detected. The guard consults migration metadata before allowing a version decrement. - Introduces idempotent pre-upgrade and post-upgrade hooks for database migrations so operators can run the same hooks in dry-run mode. Hooks include: schema-check, pg-dump (backup), apply-migrations, verify-migrations. - Adds an automated backup step (pg_dump) to the installer pre-upgrade workflow and a restore command that can be used during rollback. Backups are stored in the configured object store (S3/GCS) with a timestamped key. - Implements migration metadata files (migrations/metadata.yaml) that record reversible flag, applied_at, and checksum for each migration file; used by the downgrade guard. - Adds Terraform module variables and Helm chart annotations to pin control-plane component images and operator versions atomically during upgrades. - Adds operator-level warnings in CLI and installer logs when attempting unsafe operations and surfaces recommended rollback commands. - Adds integration tests for migration dry-run, backup/restore, and downgrade guard behavior to perf-canary and private-installer CI.

Upgrade/migration flow (high level): 1) Installer runs pre-upgrade hooks: schema-check -> pg-dump to object store -> dry-run migrations. 2) If dry-run succeeds and all migrations are reversible or flagged accordingly, installer applies migrations and marks metadata. 3) On success, post-upgrade hooks verify application connectivity. 4) If issues occur, operator can run installer rollback which triggers restore from the most recent backup and re-applies compatible schema state.

Rollback/downgrade guard behavior: - Downgrade is disallowed if any applied migration in metadata.yaml has reversible: false. - For reversible migrations, the installer will run migration rollback steps and verify schema checksum matches target. - Operators may override the guard with explicit confirmation (force flag) but a full restore is recommended and enforced when checks fail.

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for migration metadata parsing, integration test that performs upgrade->insert synthetic data->attempt downgrade (expected: blocked or restored), and e2e scenario against a test S3 bucket. CI initially failed due to a test expecting a different default PG encoding; fixed by normalizing test fixture. Final CI: pass.

Related work: ENG-5241 (Upgrade safety), ENG-5288 (Private installer resiliency). SUP-9082 tracked customer incident and requested rollback guarantees.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on migration metadata format, safety checks in hooks, and the rollback restore path. The backup uses existing installer object-store abstraction; no new cloud creds are added. The default behavior is conservative: no automatic destructive downgrades.

notes: This change is non-breaking by default but influences operator workflows. Customers using custom migration tooling should validate interoperability. Support KB and runbook updated.
risk_assessment: medium (database operations) - mitigations: pre-upgrade backups, dry-run migrations, audit logs, and explicit confirmation for force downgrades
test_plan: Unit tests for metadata parsing, integration test for upgrade->downgrade flow, e2e backup/restore against test S3, local manual validation steps documented in docs/upgrade-rollbacks.md
